newsitem.title: UK: RMC SHARES UP ON WEAK STERLING, RATE VIEWS.
newsitem.headline: RMC SHARES UP ON WEAK STERLING, RATE VIEWS.

text.p: Shares in Britain's RMC Group Plc jumped 4.5 percent on Thursday, boosted by weaker sterling and expectations for UK interest rates to hold steady for the time being, analysts and traders said.
By 1357 GMT, shares in RMC, a producer and supplier to the construction industry, were up 46p at 10.53-1/2 stg, their strongest level since November 1996.
The Bank of England hiked interest rates by 25 basis points to 7.0 percent on Thursday and signalled that they have reached levels consistent with inflation targets.
In early afternoon trading, sterling/mark was trading at 2.9665/75 against 3.0120/30 marks ahead of the news and 3.0130 in late Europe on Wednesday.

David Taylor, investment analyst at Teather and Greenwood, said the rate hike was a double bonus for RMC. The company will earn about 37 percent of its operating profits this year in Germany, and 25 percent in the UK, he said.
The stronger mark will help in translating profits from Germany back into sterling, while UK interest rates holding at 7.0 percent will not threaten Britain's housing market, he said.
"My view is that seven percent interest rates is not going to stop the UK housing market in its tracks," Taylor said.
He said fears of progressive rate hikes were raising the spectre of a downturn in the construction industry, particularly housing, in 1998.
Other currency-sensitive stocks also rallied on the selloff in sterling. Shares in engineer TI Group rose 16-1/2p to 591p and Imperial Chemical Industries Plc gained 42-1/2p to 11.05 stg.
